newsitem.title: LATVIA: SHIPPING FIRM TO APPROVE '96 RESULTS - REPORT.
newsitem.headline: SHIPPING FIRM TO APPROVE '96 RESULTS - REPORT.

text.p: The board of the Latvian Shipping Company plans to approve its 1996 results, audited by Coopers & Lybrand, on July 25, the newspaper Diena reported on Wednesday.
Latvian Shipping, currently under pivatisation, would not reveal the figures before their approval by the company's council and board, the newspaper said.
Earlier this year the company's former president, Peteris Avotinsh, said that its 1996 losses according to international accounting standards could amount to $25 million, Diena said.
In 1995, the company's losses were 51.43 million lats, according to international accounting standards. An audit conducted by Latvian accounting standards revealed a loss of 91.4 million lats.
The shipping firm has budgeted for a $20 million consolidated 1997 loss but said earlier it would revise the forecast if its good first quarter results were maintained.
The company is the world's 19th largest shipping firm. It has 41 tankers, 24 refrigerated vessels and seven dry cargo ships.
